edges.description: BGNWG’s community page lists BRH’s October and November talks. This is event sharing, not co-organization.
BGNWG’s community page lists MassRobotics’ RoboBoston and other MassRobotics-involved events.

MassRobotics published a calendar listing for Boston Robot Hackers’ September 3, 2026 Power Management in Robots meeting. This records that specific event-sharing example, not a recurring commitment, hosting arrangement or partnership.

The source says MassRobotics Women and Women in Robotics Boston have joined to strengthen their community through activities such as networking, education and mentoring. “Runs activities with” is a provisional mapping of that statement.

nodes.name: Boston Board Game Night WG
nodes.participation: Follow the mailing list and event announcements. Events move between venues; the FAQ describes a robotics-centered friends/family community rather than a general-public gaming meetup.
nodes.summary: Casual social evenings for roboticists and their friends and family, built around playing board games and meeting people. Also shares selected community events.

nodes.name: MassRobotics
nodes.participation: Use the relevant event or program signup. Some events are public; others are for partners or residents. Newsletter subscription and startup residency are different entry points.
nodes.summary: A robotics startup hub with public events, professional networking, educational programs and distinct community initiatives. Not a single uniform meetup.

nodes.name: Boston Robot Hackers
nodes.participation: The meetings page welcomes everyone, including beginners, at Artisans Asylum. The group offers an invitation-request link and a mailing list for questions and troubleshooting.
nodes.summary: A robotics learning and building community with a speaker/lightning-talk meeting and a hands-on hacking session each month.

nodes.name: Women in Robotics Boston
nodes.participation: The MassRobotics Women in Robotics page links to the Boston group and describes its joint community activities. Consult individual meetup announcements for attendance details.
nodes.summary: A community for women working in robotics or interested in entering the field, with local networking, outreach, education and mentoring.

nodes.name: Fab Hub Kendall
nodes.participation: Its site advertises free public-access hours for specified community activities and routes for workshops, volunteering and collaboration. Confirm current scheduling; this does not imply unrestricted drop-in access.
nodes.summary: The Fab Foundation’s Cambridge headquarters and flagship Fab Lab: digital fabrication, workshops, education and community-benefit projects.

nodes.name: BU RASTIC
nodes.participation: Primarily student-centered. RASTIC Certified includes seminars, workshops and projects with peer, faculty and industry connections. External visitors should confirm access for the relevant program; it is not presented as a public drop-in makerspace.
nodes.summary: BU’s student-forward robotics teaching and innovation community: collaborative projects, seminars, workshops, equipment and guidance. Included here to test university-community scope, not because it hosted BGNWG.

nodes.name: Board Game Night WG Bay Area
nodes.participation: Follow the mailing list and Bay Area chapter page for current event announcements. The FAQ describes a robotics-centered friends and family community; attendance details depend on the event.
nodes.summary: Casual social evenings for roboticists and their friends and family, built around playing board games and meeting people. Also shares selected community events.

nodes.name: Circuit Launch
nodes.participation: Browse published events for RSVP details. Workspace and equipment access require a monthly membership and equipment safety training; arrange a tour before visiting.
nodes.summary: A robotics and electronic-hardware coworking community with shared prototyping resources and events for builders and entrepreneurs.

nodes.name: HomeBrew Robotics Club
nodes.participation: Join the discussion group or attend a meeting as a guest; paid membership is optional. Check current meeting announcements before attending.
nodes.summary: A volunteer robotics club for learning, building robots, sharing projects, and exchanging technical help.
